newsitem.title: ITALY: HORSE RACING-SINGLE EMPIRE SNATCHES ITALIAN DERBY.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-SINGLE EMPIRE SNATCHES ITALIAN DERBY.

text.p: The fast finishing Single Empire, ridden by David Harrison, got up on the line to win the Italian Derby by a nose on Sunday.
It was a second Italian Derby success for English trainer Peter Chapple-Hyam who was also successful in 1993 with White Muzzle.
Second was German challenger Ungaro with Chapple-Hyam's other runner Panama City, always thereabouts under Frankie Dettori, a length further back in third.
Irish jockey Kieron Fallon was banned for 10 days and fined four million lire ($2,400) by stewards after the race.
His mount Musical Dancer finished in fifth place but he veered badly to the left and was put back to seventh after a stewards' enquiry.
It completed a bad weekend for the Irishman who received a four-day suspension on Saturday for dropping his hands and failing to ride out his mount Highborn at Doncaster.
Highborn was beaten into third place by a short head.
Fallon has not yet decided whether to appeal against Sunday's ban but it could mean him missing the Epsom Derby meeting and the start of Royal Ascot. ($ = 1666 Italian Lire)
